picture.lead: Veyro keeps teams apart and work in order. An account holds workspaces, a workspace holds projects, a project holds tasks.

b.1: Account: the plan and the billing. One person owns it.
b.2: Workspace: a private space for one team. People join by invitation only.
b.3: Project: a private board. Only people added to it see it; admins see them all.
b.4: Task: one piece of work with an assignee, a due date and a status.

r.owner: You own the account: you create workspaces, choose the plan and read the account history.
r.admin: You run a workspace: its people, its projects and every task inside it.
r.padmin: You run one project: its members and its tasks.
r.member: You see the projects you were added to and work on the tasks assigned to you.

cycle.lead: The usual path of this role, from the first day to the daily routine.

owner.1: Create your account and verify your email with the 6-digit code.
owner.2: Create your workspace. More workspaces depend on your plan.
owner.3: Invite your admins and your team by link.
owner.4: Create projects, or let admins create them.
owner.5: Keep an eye on the plan, billing and the account history.

admin.1: Accept the invitation and verify your email.
admin.2: Create projects and add the right people to each.
admin.3: Create and assign tasks, and keep the boards moving.
admin.4: Review the workspace audit trail when something changes.
admin.5: Invite or remove people as the team changes.

padmin.2: Add or remove project members and set their project role.
padmin.3: Create tasks and assign them with a due date and a category.
padmin.4: Review the work: edit, reopen with a reason, delete or restore.
padmin.5: Hand over by promoting another project admin when you need to.

member.1: Accept the invitation and sign in.
member.2: Open My tasks to see everything assigned to you, by due date.
member.3: Move your tasks: To do, In progress, In review, Done.
member.5: Ask the AI assistant when you need an answer.

owner.2: Create workspaces and choose the plan
owner.4: Delete the account (password and typed slug)

admin.2: Create, archive, delete and restore projects
admin.3: Create, assign, edit and delete any task

padmin.1: Manage the members of your project
padmin.2: Create, assign, edit, reopen and delete its tasks
padmin.3: Rename the project and edit its description

member.1: See the projects you belong to
member.2: Move the tasks assigned to you
member.4: Use the AI assistant and manage your profile

owner.1: Nothing is hidden from you, but deleting the account asks for your password.

admin.1: See billing, change the plan or read the account trail

padmin.2: Invite people to the workspace or see other projects

member.2: Cancel a task or move one that is not yours
member.3: See projects you were not added to

start.t: From sign-up to the first task
start.lead: Four short stops. You can stop at any point and pick up later.

b.1: Register with your email and a password, or continue with Google or GitHub.
b.2: Verify your email with the 6-digit code. It expires after 10 minutes and can be resent.
b.3: Choose: create your own workspace, or enter an invitation code to join one.
b.4: Create the first project and add the first task.

r.owner: You will create the workspace yourself and become its first admin.
r.admin: You usually arrive by invitation and land in a ready workspace.
r.padmin: You arrive by invitation; an admin made you project admin of your project.
r.member: You arrive by invitation, already added to your projects.

tasks.t: A task has one clear path
tasks.lead: Status changes follow rules, so the board always tells the truth.

b.1: To do, then In progress, then In review, then Done. You can step back one stage.
b.2: Cancelled is possible from any open status. Done and Cancelled are final.
b.3: To continue a finished task, an admin reopens it with a reason of at least 5 characters.
b.4: Deleted tasks wait 30 days in the trash and can be restored by an admin.

r.owner: You can do all of this on any task.
r.admin: You can do all of this on any task of your workspace.
r.padmin: You can do all of this on the tasks of your project.
r.member: You move your own tasks forward and back, but never cancel, reopen or delete.

people.t: Invite by link, locked to one email
people.lead: Nobody joins by accident. Every invitation is private and short-lived.

b.1: An admin creates an invitation link. It works only for that email address.
b.2: It is valid for 7 days and can be resent or revoked.
b.3: The admin picks the projects the person joins on the first day.
b.4: Workspace roles (Admin, Member) are separate from project roles (Project admin, Member).

r.owner: You can invite anyone and make them admin.
r.admin: You invite, resend, revoke and remove members.
r.padmin: You add workspace members to your project, you do not invite new ones.
r.member: You accept an invitation once. After that your admin keeps your access up to date.

ai.lead: Ask a question or ask for a change. Changes always wait for your confirmation.

b.1: Ask about how Veyro works, or open the quick panel inside a workspace.
b.2: Ask it to create a task and it drafts a proposal that names the project.
b.3: Nothing changes until you confirm. Confirming and rejecting never use a message.
b.4: The free plan gives 3 messages a day, renewed at 00:00 UTC.

r.owner: You can confirm task proposals in any project.
r.admin: You can confirm task proposals in any project of your workspace.
r.padmin: You can confirm task proposals for your own project.
r.member: You get answers and explanations. Creating tasks stays with project admins.

plans.lead: Limits apply to the whole account. The owner is the only person who sees billing.

b.1: Free: 1 workspace, 3 projects. Pro: 3 and 7. Enterprise: 10 and 15. Epic: unlimited workspaces, 25 projects.
b.2: Archived projects count toward the limit; deleted ones do not.
b.3: A failed payment gives 7 days of grace and everything keeps working.
b.4: After a downgrade nothing is deleted. The owner chooses which projects stay editable.

trust.t: Privacy and a history nobody can edit
trust.lead: Teams never see each other, and every important change leaves a record.

b.1: Workspaces are separate. A project you were not added to simply answers "not found".
b.2: Important changes are written to an audit trail that nobody can edit or delete.
b.3: Workspace admins read the workspace trail. Only the owner reads the account trail.
b.4: You choose your name, language and theme in your profile.

r.owner: You can read both the workspace and the account trail.
r.admin: You can read the workspace trail: who did what, and when.
r.padmin: You see your project, not the audit trail. Ask a workspace admin if you need it.
r.member: You see your own projects only. Your admins can answer "who changed this".

help.lead: Questions, a problem, billing or feedback: send a message and we read it.

b.1: Contact us works without signing in.
b.2: Your profile holds your name, language, theme and password.

Landing.hero_desc: Private workspaces, a Kanban board that enforces process, and an AI assistant that asks before it acts. Built for teams that ship.
Landing.stat_foot: AI never changes your data without your confirmation
Landing.mq_label: Everything your team does, in one workspace
Landing.wf_title: Every task has an owner, a status and a story
Landing.wf_desc: Plan the sprint, assign the work and keep the conversation next to the task, so nobody has to ask where things stand.
Landing.wf_1d: Every task has an assignee and a due date, so nothing floats.
Landing.wf_2d: To do, In progress, In review, Done. Reopening finished work needs a written reason.
Landing.wf_3d: Comments live on the task, right next to its history.
Landing.show_title: One workspace for every project, task and teammate
Landing.show_desc: See what is moving, who owns it and what needs attention, on your laptop or in your pocket.
Landing.how_title: From empty workspace to verified delivery in three moves
Landing.how_desc: No setup maze. Create the boundary, run the work, let AI assist while you stay in control.
Landing.s1_t: Create a workspace and invite your team
Landing.s1_d: Spin up an isolated workspace in one step, then invite people with the role they need. Members only ever see the projects they are assigned to.
Landing.s2_t: Execute on a board that enforces process
Landing.s2_d: Status changes follow a defined lifecycle. Reopening finished work needs a written reason, so history stays honest.
Landing.s3_d: The assistant drafts changes from your own workspace data. Nothing is written until you confirm it.
Landing.feat_title: Mastering team delivery with Veyro’s power
Landing.roles_title: Everyone sees exactly what they should
Landing.roles_desc: Roles with least privilege by default. Permissions are enforced on the server, not hidden in the interface.
Landing.r4: See every project in the workspace
Landing.roles_note: One Owner per account, who also controls billing and can delete the account.
Landing.ai_title: AI that asks before it acts
Landing.ai_desc: Ask a question about your projects. If the answer needs a change, Veyro shows you the exact mutation first. You confirm it, or nothing happens.
Landing.ai_p1: Answers come only from projects you can access
Landing.ai_p2: Every proposal needs an explicit confirmation
Landing.ai_p3: Confirmed changes run atomically and are audit-logged

Landing.p1_d: Your team’s data stays inside your workspace. Nobody outside it can see that a project even exists.
Landing.p2_d: Lifecycles, reasons and audit events make the history of the work believable.
Landing.p3_d: AI saves time on drafting and balancing. People keep the final say.
Landing.contact_desc: Questions about the product, a pilot for your team, or feedback. We read everything.
Landing.ct1_d: How Veyro would work for your team
Landing.ct2_d: Try a private workspace with real projects
Landing.ct3_d: Tell us what to improve next
